answer: Each identity burns 60 copper into a lagoon sink, locks a 40 bond, and files one key-signed receipt per epoch. The lagoon publishes an echo list of burns; auditors recompute its total, and standing identities cannot exceed burns divided by 60, so excess filings are dropped. Each fake still costs a fresh 60 burn plus 40 bond, 100 total, so 1,000 fakes cost 100,000, since one burn backs one identity. Registry inflation fails: identities without a matching burn are cut at the cap. An honest agent pays 100 once and recovers its 40 bond after a clean epoch.
